summary.text: Veronica Paiz is the Democratic state representative for Michigan House District 10, which she has held since January 1, 2025, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said the district includes the Grosse Pointes, Harper Woods and parts of Detroit's east side, and that she served on the Harper Woods City Council from 2015 to 2022.

paragraphs.text: Veronica Paiz was born in San Antonio, Texas, and earned a bachelor's degree from Wayne State University in 1980 and a graduate degree from New York University in 1992.

Ballotpedia lists her past service on the Michigan Municipal League's Municipal Services and Elections Committees, as director of Casa de Unidad, and as an executive board member of the Michigan Democratic Party Hispanic Latino Caucus.
In the Ballotpedia survey, she said that she and her husband have lived in Harper Woods since 1999 and that she previously served on the city's library and parks and recreation boards.
Paiz was assigned to the House Agriculture Committee and the Financial Services Committee for 2025-2026, according to Ballotpedia.

She said in the survey that she is Minority Vice Chair of the House Agriculture Committee and was named 2025 Legislator of the Year by the Michigan Library Association for her "Right to Read" legislation.

She won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 71.6 percent of the vote over Ryan M. Nelson and Andrew Cyburt, and faces Republican Peter Ochs and Piper Smith of the Working Class Party in the general election.
Paiz named housing, environment and water, senior citizens, food, and civil rights and social justice as the policy areas she is most passionate about.
